literal: Limit having known with him who eats pleasure like will stand excessive great with him who has food disease.
translation: Just as health stays with the man who eats knowing his limit, disease stays with the glutton who eats excessively.
modern: தன் செரிமான அளவை அறிந்து உண்பவனிடம் இன்பம் நிலைத்திருப்பது போல, மிக அதிகமாக உண்பவனிடம் நோய் நிலைத்து நிற்கும்.
explanation: The word iḻivu here means the limit or measure of one's digestion. The couplet draws a direct parallel between two states of being. Just as well-being and pleasure remain with the person who eats mindfully within their limits, illness takes up permanent residence in the person who consumes an excessive amount of food. The contrast between iṉpam (pleasure or health) and nōy (disease) highlights the physical consequences of dietary habits.
